title: Control Board Communication Fault
shortDescription: The main control board has lost communication with the user interface or peripheral boards.
fullDescription:
F01 on a Hotpoint dryer indicates a communication failure between the main electronic control board (PCB) and either the user interface/display board or an auxiliary motor controller. The dryer typically stops mid-cycle and refuses to start new programs.

This error is common on Whirlpool EMEA platform dryers shared with Indesit and Ariston. It is usually caused by loose wiring harnesses, oxidised connectors, moisture ingress, or a failed control PCB. Occasionally a firmware corruption or voltage spike triggers the same fault.

causes.cause: Loose or disconnected wiring harness between PCB and UI

fixSteps.title: Power cycle the dryer
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the dryer from the outlet for 10 minutes then reconnect.

fixSteps.title: Inspect wiring harnesses
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the top panel and check all ribbon cables between the main PCB and user interface board for secure seating.

fixSteps.title: Replace main control board
fixSteps.instruction: If reseating connectors does not resolve the fault, replace the main PCB with a matching part number.

whenToCallPro: Call a professional if reseating connectors does not clear the code or if you are uncomfortable working with mains electronics.

faq.a: Yes, start with a 10-minute power cycle which clears transient faults.

faq.q: Is the dryer safe to use with F01?
faq.a: No, do not attempt to run cycles until the communication fault is resolved.

title: Motor Tacho Signal Fault
shortDescription: The control board is not receiving a valid speed signal from the drum motor tachometer.
fullDescription:
F02 indicates the PCB cannot read the motor's tachogenerator (tacho) signal, which is used to regulate drum speed. The dryer will either refuse to spin the drum or stop shortly after starting.

Causes include a failed tacho coil, worn motor brushes, a snapped drive belt that leaves the motor unloaded, or a broken wire in the motor harness. On Hotpoint condenser and heat-pump models the same code can appear if the motor control triac on the PCB fails.

fixSteps.title: Check drum rotation by hand
fixSteps.instruction: Open the door and rotate the drum. It should turn smoothly with slight belt resistance.

fixSteps.title: Inspect drive belt
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the top and front panel to access the belt. Replace if snapped or stretched.

fixSteps.title: Test tacho coil
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance across the tacho coil terminals on the motor; typical reading is 100-300 ohms.

whenToCallPro: Call a professional if belt replacement does not resolve the issue or the motor requires replacement.

faq.a: Not always — a snapped belt can trigger F02 because the motor spins without load.

title: NTC Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The NTC temperature sensor is reading out of range (open or short circuit).
fullDescription:
F03 indicates that the negative temperature coefficient (NTC) thermistor used to monitor drum or exhaust air temperature is reporting an impossible value to the control board.

On Hotpoint dryers the NTC is mounted near the condenser or heater housing. A failed sensor, a disconnected harness, or a blocked airflow path causing extreme temperatures can all trigger F03. Replacement sensors are inexpensive and straightforward to swap.

fixSteps.title: Unplug and access sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the rear panel to expose the NTC near the heating element or condenser.

fixSteps.title: Test NTC resistance
fixSteps.instruction: At room temperature the NTC should read approximately 10-50 kOhms. Replace if open or shorted.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the sensor tests good but F03 persists — the PCB may be at fault.
videoSearchQuery: Hotpoint dryer F03 NTC sensor replacement

faq.q: How do I test an NTC?
faq.a: Measure resistance at room temperature; a reading of infinity or zero indicates a faulty sensor.

title: Pressure Switch Fault
shortDescription: The condensate pressure switch or level sensor is reporting an abnormal state.
fullDescription:
F04 indicates that the pressure switch (or the analogue pressure transducer on newer boards) has reported a state the PCB considers invalid — for example signalling full when the condenser tank is empty.

Common root causes include a blocked pressure hose, a faulty switch diaphragm, or a full condenser water container that has not been emptied. On heat-pump dryers a blocked drain pump can also flag F04.

fixSteps.title: Empty the condenser tank
fixSteps.instruction: Pull out and empty the front water container, then reseat fully.

fixSteps.title: Inspect pressure hose
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the top panel and inspect the clear hose between the sump and pressure switch for kinks or debris.

fixSteps.title: Replace pressure switch
fixSteps.instruction: If the hose is clear and switch fails to click when blown into, replace it.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the pump or sump requires disassembly.

faq.q: Why does F04 come back after emptying?
faq.a: A kinked pressure hose often traps water and keeps the switch closed.

title: Condensate Drain Pump Fault
shortDescription: The drain pump is not moving condensate water from the sump to the tank.
fullDescription:
F05 indicates that the condensate pump is either electrically faulty, blocked by lint, or its hose is obstructed. The machine typically stops and flashes F05 early in the cycle.

On heat-pump models this code can also appear when the sump filter is heavily clogged, starving the pump of water flow. Cleaning the filter often resolves F05 without parts.

fixSteps.title: Clean sump filter
fixSteps.instruction: Open the front filter access and remove all lint from the sump.

fixSteps.title: Access pump
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the front panel and kick plate to access the pump housing.

fixSteps.title: Test and replace pump
fixSteps.instruction: Check winding resistance (~180 ohms). Replace if open or seized.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the pump is integrated into a sealed sump.

faq.q: Can I use the dryer if I empty the tank manually?
faq.a: Not recommended — standing water can short electronics.

title: Door Lock Fault
shortDescription: The door interlock switch is not confirming door closed status to the PCB.
fullDescription:
F06 means the control board does not see a closed signal from the door safety switch. The dryer will refuse to start any cycle.

Typical causes are a misaligned door catch, a worn interlock microswitch, or broken wires in the door hinge loom. Replacement interlock assemblies are inexpensive.
symptoms: Door appears closed but F06 shows

fixSteps.title: Firmly close door
fixSteps.instruction: Press the door firmly and listen for a solid click.

fixSteps.title: Inspect latch
fixSteps.instruction: Examine the striker and catch for wear or bent brackets.

fixSteps.title: Replace interlock
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the door trim and swap the microswitch assembly.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if replacement does not clear the code and wiring must be traced.

faq.a: No, it is a safety interlock and the dryer refuses to run until resolved.

title: Heater Fault
shortDescription: The heating element is not reaching target temperature or has failed open.
fullDescription:
F07 is raised when the dryer fails to heat the drum air within the expected time window. On condenser and vented Hotpoint models this usually points to a burnt-out heater or tripped thermal cut-out.

On heat-pump models F07 can indicate a compressor that is not pressurising the refrigerant loop. Lint build-up on the heater and blocked airflow are the most common DIY-fixable causes.

fixSteps.title: Clean filters and condenser
fixSteps.instruction: Clean both the lint filter and condenser unit (if accessible).

fixSteps.title: Test heater continuity
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power and measure resistance across the heater — typical value 20-40 ohms.

fixSteps.title: Reset or replace TOC
fixSteps.instruction: Press the manual reset on the thermal cut-out; replace if it does not hold.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro for heat-pump compressor issues or if heater replacement requires stripping the cabinet.

faq.q: Why does the TOC keep tripping?
faq.a: Almost always due to restricted airflow from lint build-up.

title: Heater Relay Stuck Closed
shortDescription: The heater relay on the main PCB has welded closed and cannot switch off heat.
fullDescription:
F08 indicates the PCB has detected that the heater relay contacts are stuck closed — the heater continues to draw current even when the board commands it off. This is a safety-critical fault.

Over time inrush current from the heating element can weld the relay contacts. The main PCB must normally be replaced, though experienced technicians sometimes replace the relay component on the board.

causes.cause: Welded heater relay on main PCB

fixSteps.title: Disconnect power immediately
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the dryer to prevent overheating and possible fire risk.

fixSteps.title: Test heater for short
fixSteps.instruction: Measure heater resistance and continuity to chassis to rule out a shorted element.

fixSteps.title: Replace main PCB
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the control board with a matching service part.

whenToCallPro: Always call a professional — F08 is a fire safety concern.

faq.a: Yes, stop using the dryer immediately and seek professional repair.

title: Software ROM Error
shortDescription: The PCB firmware image has failed its integrity check at power on.
fullDescription:
F09 means the control board cannot validate its firmware ROM. It may appear after a power cut, surge, or factory programming issue.

A 10-minute hard power cycle occasionally clears a transient checksum fault, but in most cases the PCB must be reprogrammed or replaced by service.

fixSteps.title: Replace PCB
fixSteps.instruction: If code persists the PCB must be swapped for a programmed replacement.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro — firmware repair typically requires a pre-programmed service board.

faq.q: Can I reflash the PCB at home?
faq.a: No, programming tools and images are restricted to service agents.

title: EEPROM Memory Checksum Error
shortDescription: The PCB cannot read valid configuration data from its EEPROM.
fullDescription:
F10 indicates a checksum mismatch in the non-volatile memory where model configuration and user preferences are stored. The dryer is unsafe to operate until valid configuration is restored.

This fault is typically caused by EEPROM wear after many thousands of cycles or by electromagnetic interference during a write. Service technicians can sometimes re-initialise the EEPROM using a diagnostic cable, but most repairs require a replacement PCB.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Try a 15-minute power cycle to see if the EEPROM re-initialises.

fixSteps.title: Replace PCB
fixSteps.instruction: If the code persists the control board must be replaced.

whenToCallPro: Always call a pro — PCB replacement and configuration required.

faq.q: Why did F10 appear after a storm?
faq.a: A lightning-induced surge can corrupt EEPROM writes in progress.
